_about: Reader-facing places. Claude-owned. x/y are map coordinates in the site's 400x300 map; on_page means the name has appeared in saga/chronicle/. Descriptions must be supported by the chronicle. Map-only places (on_page false) show as names on the map and nothing else. Optional per place: label (map text, defaults to name), anchor (start|middle|end for region labels), label_below (true puts a marker's label under it), label_right (true puts it to the right), draw:false (no marker). For a terrain label (a region, river, road or the like): arc (a number: it bows along a gentle curve, + up, - down) big (true: the wide-spaced capitals of a broad country) and lines (2: the first word over the rest). route is a list of place ids or [x, y] waypoints, and null starts a new leg (the legs before the last are drawn fainter); the map draws Darrow at the route's end, so extend it whenever he moves (the build refuses a route that does not end at his place when that place has a marker). Optional picture (only for a place already on the page): image (a path under saga/art/, e.g. places/<id>.webp), image_alt (what it shows, for screen readers), image_caption, and image_focus ("50% 50%": the centre of the 16:9 crop); the site shows it in the codex entry, tap to enlarge. Optional aliases: other words the Chronicle uses for the place ("the Steps"); the story's first mention of any of them in a scene links to the place's Codex entry with a preview.

places.name: Saint Ysolde's
places.subtitle: the House of Menders
places.description: The House of Menders at the top of the Thousand Steps, which takes the ones the lowland surgeons cannot fix and do not want to watch. Bells ring the hours; the air smells of snow and sulphur and boiled linen. Its infirmary hall is a long double row of cots, and the far ones hold the ones who no longer speak. Its gate opens on a court, with a wicket in the leaf for a courier's paper and a gatehouse whose window looks down on the Steps. Below the gate, where the springs steam on the lower terrace, the Confessors have made their fire.
places.image_alt: Saint Ysolde's: a grey stone house with a bell tower and lit windows on a snowy cliff above a sea of cloud, the Thousand Steps switchbacking down the cliff face, jagged snow peaks behind, and a thin road crossing a white valley far below.
places.image_caption: Saint Ysolde's above the cloud, and the Thousand Steps below it.

places.name: The Thousand Steps
places.description: The switchback stair cut into the cliff below Saint Ysolde's, with cloud on one side and a wind that comes round the shoulder of the mountain with a knife in it. Everyone says a thousand. Wren has counted eleven hundred and seventeen.

places.name: The lower terrace
places.subtitle: below the gate of Saint Ysolde's
places.description: The grey below the House's gate where the springs steam: the law's ground and nobody's, Confessor Ivo Marrant said, and made his camp there in the snow with four grey cloaks, in sight of the gatehouse window. The first of their fires was built while the court was still standing in the snow.

places.name: The winch-house
places.subtitle: at the foot of the Steps
places.description: At the foot of the Thousand Steps, where the stair comes out of the cloud at the valley floor: a grey block with a thread of smoke of its own, and the cage the House's loads come up by. Rae Thorne's cart stands beside it with its shafts up and two oxen in the snow, standing the way oxen stand, as if they had been told to wait and meant to do it all winter. The grey cloaks came in at it three bells early, six riders, their cart and a censer, and one of them sat down on Rae's cart and put his boots up on the board. One grey cloak keeps it while the rest camp on the lower terrace.
places.image_alt: The winch-house: a low grey stone house with an icicled, snow-heavy slate roof and a thin thread of chimney smoke, built against the foot of a sheer cliff; a fire glows in its open door, a rope runs from a drum on its wall up into the cloud, an iron cage loaded with sacks waits beside it, a stair climbs the cliff in switchbacks, and two shaggy oxen stand in the snow by an empty wooden cart.
places.image_caption: The winch-house where the stair comes out of the cloud, and Thorne's cart and two oxen in the snow.

places.name: Coldmere
places.description: Rae Thorne's village, on the Holloway below the mountain, where the road dips to a tarn and the fog comes off the water. Its bell-house stands with its back to the tarn, and it has a mill, a fair and a rope rhyme of its own. Its inn, square and yellow at the water's edge, is the only one in Coldmere and the best on the Holloway, and Rae's uncle keeps it: everything that goes up or down the road goes through his taproom. There the Confessors' list of the Faithless was read aloud, and he filled the reader's cup between the names. A Lance's column coming up the road made camp on the green by the water.
places.image_alt: Coldmere at night in falling snow: a snow-roofed inn of stone and dark timber with a blank sign and warm-lit windows, a crowd standing still in the taproom behind the big window while a hooded figure in a grey cloak reads from a long paper. Grey horses stand tied at a rail. In the foreground an ox-cart loaded with sacks, a lantern hanging from it and its cloaked driver seen from behind, pulls away onto the dark road. Below, snowy roofs run down to a black, half-frozen lake under a wall of mountains and cloud.
places.image_caption: The inn at Coldmere, the night the list was read, and a cart going out into the dark ahead of the grey cloaks.

places.name: The Holloway
places.subtitle: the road
places.description: The road below the Steps, from the winch-house at their foot down past Coldmere and its tarn to the Wend landing, and on to Calden. From the infirmary window it is a brown thread across a white field. Below the seventh milestone it runs deep between its banks, and at the Elbow it turns back on itself with room for one cart. Carters sing salt on it to their bells, no two to the same tune. Six grey riders and a cart came up it with a smudge of smoke above them; then a Lance's column under a banner that was not grey, and the Confessors' cart went down to meet it.

places.name: The drove road
places.description: A track between two walls that leaves the Holloway above Coldmere and runs north round the far side of the tarn, past a shepherds' fold on the north shore, then down off the moor's shoulder to a hamlet with a bell-post where the tracks cross, and on along the turnip country. Rae turned her cart onto it rather than drive into a Lance on the march. Every door on it opened to the carter, Wren counted, until the company was on her cart.

places.name: The Wend landing
places.label: Wend landing
places.subtitle: where the Holloway meets the river
places.description: Where a barge on the Wend unloads for the carts on the Holloway, and where the price of salt is set. The salt-cart that took Darrow and Hollis on to the Steps left its load at the landing to make room for them, and Rae once carted a nailed crate off a barge there to the lower door at Calden: a day and a half on the road.

places.name: The Lowmarch
places.description: Darrow's country: he had the fastest feet in it, and its children count the lances in a rhyme. Its villages have bell-houses, from whose steps the Crown's heralds read that the Grace had left the knights of Harrow Ford, and its surgeons sent him north.
places.image_alt: A Lowmarch village on a wet afternoon: thatched timber cottages around a puddled green, flat fields of green and gold divided by hedgerows running to a low horizon under grey cloud. A grey stone bell-house with a bronze bell in its open belfry stands at the centre, and on its steps a herald reads from an unrolled parchment to villagers holding their hats, children sitting on a stone wall. In the foreground an ox-cart carrying hurt men wrapped in blankets rolls along the muddy road.
places.image_caption: A bell-house in the Lowmarch: the herald on its steps, and a cart going by.

places.name: The river Wend
places.description: Cold and fast, brown with three days of rain off the hills at midsummer. It runs past Harrow Ford at the edge of the Thornwild, and it carried the Ninth downstream like driftwood. Loads come off a barge on it at the Wend landing.
places.label: The Wend

places.name: Harrow Ford
places.description: A crossing of the Wend at the edge of the Thornwild, with standing stones on the far bank. Here, halfway across, the Grace went out of the Ninth, and Darrow's knee gave way with no blade near it.
places.image_alt: Harrow Ford on a misty morning: a high, fast, mud-brown river churning white over stones. On the near bank, seen from behind, mounted knights in mail and helms hold long lances with sodden pennons, and beside them an ox-cart carries a great slab of black stone in an iron frame. Across the water, tall grey standing stones lean on a gravel shore where a ragged line of fighters with spears waits at the edge, ox-carts piled with bundles and old people behind them, a goat among them, under the dark old trees of a forest.
places.image_caption: The Lances on the west bank, and the clans drawn up among the standing stones.

places.name: The Thornwild
places.description: The forest beyond the far bank of the Wend, home of the clans. In the dark under its trees a line of grey, armored figures stood very still while the river screamed.

places.name: Calden
places.description: Where the Oathspire stands, and where the Faithless are told they may kneel anew. Somewhere in a warm room there, Darrow believes, his name was written first on a list.

places.name: The Oathspire
places.subtitle: in Calden
places.description: In Calden. The heralds say the Faithless will be received there with mercy and permitted to kneel anew; Maelis calls that the Crown's way, and fast.

places.name: Edgemoor
places.description: The place in Darrow's name as the Reckoning writes it: Ser Darrow of Edgemoor.

places.name: The Greywater
places.description: The mountains north of the Lowmarch into which the surgeons sent him; Saint Ysolde's stands above the cloud on a shoulder of them.
places.label: The Greywater
